title: Wampmissic
summary: Wampmissic is a tract of land and large swamp in Brookhaven, between Yaphank and Manor stations on the Long Island Rail Road. The name is interpreted as a place of chestnut trees.
history_content: The name belongs to the interior Brookhaven landscape later associated with the Manor of St. George and Smith-family land records. Dated references appear in the historic moments below.
translation_content:
Wampmissic is interpreted as place of chestnut trees, from words connected with chestnut tree and a locative ending.

Why Place Names Matter

“Traditional names can be officially recognised and recorded, which enables the story and culture of the local Aboriginal community to be shared.”

— NSW Government, Aboriginal place naming (n.d.), page introduction
preservation_content: Wampmissic preserves a plant-based placename tied to a swamp landscape and the chestnut trees remembered there before nineteenth-century fire damage.
whereintheworld_content: Blue/general approximate marker between Yaphank and Manorville. This is not an exact swamp boundary, deed tract, or station coordinate.
